newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour would create new media regulator.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour would create new media regulator.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party would create a new and powerful communications regulator to oversee the world of telecoms and media if it wins the election set for May 1.
The creation of Ofcom - the Office of Communications - would be the central plank of Labour policy for the media and telecommunications industries.
It would combine the functions of telecoms regulator Oftel and the Independent Television Commission (ITC), the body which oversees commercial television in Britain.

However, Labour distanced itself from suggestions that the new body would assume responsibility for policing the licence-funded BBC radio and television broadcasting corporation after that idea sparked controversy.
Labour has also indicated that it will move away from specific media ownership limits contained in the 1996 Broadcasting Act legislation.
It favours the increased use of public interest tests to determine whether a specific media acquisition should be cleared, rather than the application of pre-set limits.
Under the current rules, newspaper groups with over 20 percent of national circulation are barred from ownership of a commercial terrestrial television (ITV) channel.
That rules out Mirror Group and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp from owning ITV channels.

The Labour-supporting Mirror Group has argued long and hard against the rule. It claims that it is effectively the only group disadvantaged as News Corp already has substantial television interests through its 40 percent stake in satellite broadcaster BSkyB, which is not affected by the Act.
